abstract: AI-driven Virtual Influencers (VIs) are increasingly deployed as persuasive agents in digital environments, yet the mechanisms of human-agent interaction driving their effectiveness remain theoretically ambiguous. Existing VI research is fragmented, producing contradictory findings that obscure how persuasion operates when the source is non-human. To address this, this study identifies critical success factors and examines their structural relationships and relative importance using a multi-method approach (SLR, Fuzzy DEMATEL, and Fuzzy DANP) grounded in Lasswell's Communication Model. The analysis suggests a distinct hierarchy in which source-related factors occupy the primary position and exert the strongest perceived influence on the remaining endorsement-related factors. Notably, expert evaluations indicate that structural credibility carries greater relative importance than visual fidelity, while attitude emerges as a central structural mechanism rather than a static outcome. Theoretically, the findings contribute an expert-informed structural perspective on VI endorsement by illustrating how Lasswell's communication components may be structurally related and by synthesising complementary insights from Source Credibility, the CASA paradigm, and Uncanny Valley theory into a coherent interpretive framework. Collectively, this perspective may help designers and strategists better understand the VI ecosystem and inform decisions to minimise deployment risks while enhancing system acceptance and value.

ur.tldr: 聚焦虚拟影响者代言的说服力，以结构分析考察影响者、代言内容与消费者反应之间的作用路径，识别代言有效性的关键关系。核心判断是虚拟影响者的说服力取决于相关因素的结构性匹配，而非单纯依赖新奇呈现，为品牌筛选虚拟代言人及设计代言内容提供依据。

title: What makes virtual influencers persuasive? A structural analysis of endorsement effectiveness
title_zh: 虚拟网红为何具有说服力：代言有效性的结构分析
